answer: Clique-Density Admission. Each agent node tracks its local neighbor graph and requires new peers to already sit in a dense subgraph: at least k mutual neighbors within two hops. A genuine cluster forms a trellis of overlapping triangles that is cheap to maintain but hard to fabricate at scale. Isolated agents cannot forge those shared links without persuading many existing nodes to accept them. An attacker must recruit and sustain a nebula of interlinked identities, paying the full hosting and connection cost for each one, before any single identity clears the density threshold.
